# Fixed top nav — mobile layout issues
File: `portfolio/index.html` (single-file site).
Repro: serve the folder, then `window.lab.jump(p)` in the console to seek.

## Background: the mechanism behind all of these
`#idbar` ([:228](index.html:228)) is `position: fixed` at top-left with `max-width: calc(100vw - 172px)` on `≤760px`.
Those 172px are reserved to clear the `#skip` button.
At 375px that leaves 203px for content that naturally wants 415px, so it wraps.

The one non-obvious fact that unlocks it: `skipEl.classList.toggle("off", pT > 0.838)` ([:4677](index.html:4677)) — `#skip` is already hidden before the outro starts, so during the outro those 172px reserve space for nothing.
That's what makes a state-dependent width cap safe.
## ✅ FIXED — Nav overlapped outro headline (the reported bug)
At 375px the nav wrapped to 3 lines (72px tall) and covered "the complexity was never in the rules" plus the credentials line.
Three changes
all inside `@media (max-width: 760px)`:
Hid the name on mobile ([:231](index.html:231), markup [:281](index.html:281)) — wrapped in `.who`.
It's already carried by the hero, the outro headline, and the resume sheet header.
Saves 100px.
Released the width cap when `#skip` is gone ([:232](index.html:232)) — `body:has(#skip.off) #idbar { max-width: calc(100vw - 24px) }`.
Positioned dependents off a measured `--strip` ([:224](index.html:224), [:234](index.html:234)) fed by a `ResizeObserver` ([:4353](index.html:4353)).
Verified 320/375/760px, 18 scroll points, zero collisions.
Desktop byte-identical.
> ⚠️ Worth knowing: my first attempt hardcoded `--strip: 66px/46px`.
It passed everything at 375px and silently failed at 320px, where the strip still needs two lines.
Strip height is a function of width × skip-state × font metrics, which CSS can't compute — hence the JS measurement.
The remaining CSS value (`88px`) is a no-JS fallback set to the tallest case, so it fails safe.
## ✅ FIXED — Nav overlapped the chapter caption during the story
`#phase` was pinned at `top: 46px` — exactly a one-line nav's bottom edge, i.e. the layout assumed the nav never wrapped.
The wrapped nav had been sitting on the chapter text throughout the whole story (worse before, at 3 lines).
Now derives from `--strip`.
Same root cause, so I folded it in.
## 🔴 OPEN — Landscape phones / short windows, >760px
Headline is overlapped by the nav.
Different mechanism: the nav is a clean single line, but `#outro` is taller than `max-height: 94vh`, so it pins to the top of the viewport and slides under the fixed nav.
Confirmed pre-existing (media query inactive at 812px
`#outro` padding is still the original `8px 4px`
my changes are provably inert there).

Why I left it: the fix is a top offset on `#outro` outside the media query, and at 1280×800 the outro is already scroll-capped (`h2` top 32 vs nav bottom 45.5) — it escapes visually only because the headline is centered and the viewport is wide.
So a general fix nudges desktop, which was explicitly out of scope for me.
Suggested fix: height-gated rather than width-gated — e.g.
`@media (max-height: 560px) { #outro { padding-top: 52px } }`.
Never fires at 1280×800, so desktop stays untouched.
Not fully mapped: I verified 812×375 breaks and 1280×800 is clear.

## 🟡 OPEN (cosmetic) — Leading separator on wrapped line
During the story at 375px the second line begins `· email` — the `·` wraps with the following link instead of clinging to `linkedin`.
Fix is either nowrap-wrapping each link+separator pair, or moving `#idbar` to `inline-flex` with `gap` and dropping the literal `·` characters.
Markup churn for a cosmetic issue.
## 🟡 OPEN (latent) — `172px` is coupled to `#skip`'s label text
`#skip` measures 137.8px wide at mobile ("skip to summary →") + `right: 10px` = ~148px, so the 172px reserve has ~24px of slack.
Editing the skip button's label will silently re-wrap the mobile nav.
Nothing links the two numbers.
Could be made robust by measuring `#skip` the same way `--strip` measures the bar.
## ℹ️ Note — new `:has()` dependency
The fix uses `body:has(#skip.off)`.
Supported everywhere current (Chrome 105+, Safari 15.4+, Firefox 121+)
verified via `CSS.supports`.
If the browser floor is older, the `88px` fallback keeps it non-colliding, just less tight.
## ⚠️ Methodology warning for whoever picks this up
Naive bounding-box overlap tests produce false positives on this page.

`#outro h2` is a full-width block with centered text, so its box passes under the left-aligned nav while the glyphs sit well clear — my first check flagged "overlap" at 1280px where there is visibly none.
Use `Range.getBoundingClientRect()` over the text contents to get the real glyph box.

Also: rAF is suspended when the browser pane is hidden, so `ResizeObserver`/rAF-based settling won't fire in automated checks — dispatch a synthetic `resize` to force `--strip` to update synchronously.

So, back to the open question: does a `Node` know about its filesystem, or just about a disk?
The reason I'd push for "just a disk": `Ext2` holds `StrongRef<Node> root`, so a `StrongRef<Ext2>` inside `Node` closes a refcount cycle that nothing will ever collect.
A `Node` needs to read arbitrary blocks — that's a `StrongRef<BlockIO>` and a block size, nothing more.
Give it those two and the cycle can't form.

The counter-argument worth hearing: if you later want a shared block cache or an inode table cache living in `Ext2`, a `Node` with no route back to its filesystem can't reach it, and you'd end up threading a cache pointer through anyway.
`WeakRef<Ext2>` buys that option now at the cost of a promote on each use.

GitHub cannot delete a pull request.
There's no DELETE endpoint, and it isn't an admin feature.
Closing, archiving, and repo-deletion are the only options, and none of them removes a `pull/` ref except deleting the repository.
So "make it complete that way" isn't reachable at the PR level.
